Creedence Clearwater Revival: Lookin' Out My Back Door

"Lookin' Out My Back Door" was a direct tribute to the Bakersfield Sound, a form of music that influenced Fogerty and the CCR sound. Buck Owens, one of the architects of the Bakersfield Sound, is even mentioned in the song's lyrics.

The song's lyrics, filled with colorful, dream-like imagery, led some to believe that the song was about drugs. According to the drug theory, the "flying spoon" in the song was a reference to a cocaine or heroin spoon, and the crazy animal images were an acid trip. Fogerty, however, has stated in interviews that the song was actually written for his then three-year-old son, Josh. Fogerty has also said that the reference to a parade passing by was inspired by the Dr. Seuss book And to Think That I Saw It on Mulberry Street.

It shouldn't, perhaps can't, be done traditionally. Even behind Tor and I2P we have to run web servers to handle the load, and we can be deanonymized when they fail, while protecting the attackers. There's no point in all this just to move mostly-static data around.

Freenet/GNUnet worked with their data stores decades ago. Syndie is a transport-agnostic data store of the same style, which was popular on I2P for a short time, but it was overcomplicated and suffered from the Java disease of all the projects of that era. I2P supports BitTorrent well. ZeroNet is built on BitTorrent-like technology, and works with Tor, and its users frequently store large files on IPFS. dTube and a few other sites use IPFS or Web Torrents to lighten and distribute the load of large files. OpenBazaar uses the DHT, and will eventually be Tor compatible, if it isn't already. NNTPchan is a throwback: a modern image BBS in a federated design, backed by the old news protocol.

The "primitives" available are higher-level than they used to be: DHT and IPFS seem to be especially adaptable because they're such simple data stores. And Torrents are so widely implemented now, even in browsers, that BitChute makes sense. ZeroNet already has a Voat lookalike "zerovoat" and a chan lookalike "zerochan," while NNTPchan is highly available from eepsites and hidden services.

Unfortunately, users chase stupid shit. Facebook, Discord, and Slack are horrible in performance, privacy, and usability yet all wildly popular, where other services and software would work better. Then there's Mastadon, masquerading as a federated microblog, where most servers subscribe to an anti-free-speech kill list ("free speech zone" is a reason to block an instance) which fractures the network. Google killed DejaNews and Reader, which effectively spelled the death of NNTP and RSS/Atom for the masses who lick the Alphabet agency taint.

In the end, we're lucky Voat is dying slowly. It gives us a chance to regroup. But what I can recommend today as backup meeting places are no less centralized (8ch.net/voat/) or are barely usable (ZeroNet). Still, it's better than it used to be.
